content.title: Today’s NYT Strands Hints, Spangram, Answers: Sunday, March 22 (Trademarked No More)
content.text: StrandsNYTLooking for Saturday’s Strands hints, spangram and answers? You can find them here:ForbesToday’s NYT Strands Hints, Spangram, Answers: Saturday, March 21 (Sniff Sniff)By Paul TassiThis is probably one of the hardest Strands I’ve seen in a while, one where I don’t know how you’d complete it without lots of hints or an answer guide like this.How To Play StrandsThe New York Times’ Strands puzzle is a play on the classic word search. It’s in beta for now, which means it’ll only stick around if enough people play it every day.There’s a new game of Strands to play every day. The game will present you with a six by eight grid of letters. The aim is to find a group of words that have something in common, and you’ll get a clue as to what that theme is. When you find a theme word, it will remain highlighted in blue.PROMOTEDYou’ll also need to find a special word called a spangram. This tells you what the words have in common. The spangram links two opposite sides of the board. While the theme words will not be a proper name, the spangram can be a proper name. When you find the spangram, it will remain highlighted in yellow.Be warned: You’ll need to be on your toes.“Some themes are fill-in-the-blank phrases. They may also be steps in a process, items that all belong to the same category, synonyms or homophones,” The New York Times notes. “Just as she varies the difficulty of Wordle puzzles within a week, [Wordle and Strands editor Tracy] Bennett plans to throw Strands solvers curveballs every once in a while.”MORE FOR YOUWhat Is Today’s Strands Hint?Time to do the NYT hint and then my own hint after that:Trademarked no moreAnd mine is:Now common words Email Address Today’s NYT Strands Opening LettersHere are the first two letters of all the words if you don’t want the entire thing just yet.THDUZIESASWhat Are Today’s Strands Answers?Now we begin the answer portion of the program which is the spangram and the full list of the other answers, the spangram is:GENERICTERMSHere it is on the page, and read on:StrandsNYTThe answers are:THERMOSDUMPSTERZIPPERESCALATORASPIRINStrandsNYTIf you’re someone who goes for perfect no-hint Strands runs, I have no idea what you’d do here. While non-trademarked things can be somewhat easy to think of, the list we have here requires extremely specific knowledge of what was a trademarked term in the first place, and I knew exactly…zero of these were. This puzzle is more about teaching me something new (well, five things) rather than drawing on some sort of existing knowledge that is close to impossible to already have.
